**Not ready to publish.** One sentence breaks the brand policy.

**Claims check**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "reduces anxiety" | Unsupported. Health claims of any kind are banned (section 3). |
| "helps you sleep" | Unsupported. This is also a health claim, and a sleep-benefit claim on a tea is the kind regulators and ad platforms look for. |
| "caffeine-free" | Product fact, fine. |
| "gentle, honeyed" | Flavour description, fine. |
| "Certified organic by the Soil Association" | Allowlisted, exact wording. |
| "20 plastic-free tea bags" | "Plastic-free" is allowlisted. The count is a product fact, fine as long as the product team confirms 20 for this tea. |

No problems with banned words, urgency, superlatives, invented numbers or UK spelling.

**Suggested fix**

> Chamomile and Lemon Balm. A gentle, honeyed, caffeine-free blend for an unhurried evening cup. Certified organic by the Soil Association. 20 plastic-free tea bags.

This drops the health claims and keeps everything else. If you want a "compostable" mention, use the exact allowlisted wording: "plastic-free and home compostable".

The corrected version still needs Sam's approval, as all public content does.

```json
{"issues": [{"quote": "reduces anxiety", "type": "health_claim"}, {"quote": "helps you sleep", "type": "health_claim"}], "publish": false}
```
